title: Particle Detection - Delamination Detection on Zeta-388
subtitle: Post-Planarization Quality Validation for 28nm Node Manufacturing
author: Dr. Yuki Tanaka

sections.1_OBJECTIVE:
This test case validates the capability of the Zeta-388 system to detect and classify Delamination defects during post-planarization inspection at the 28nm technology node. The test is conducted at Hsinchu Fab 15 to ensure manufacturing quality standards are met for 300mm wafer production.

The primary objective is to verify that the inspection system meets the required detection sensitivity and classification accuracy for Delamination defects that are critical to yield at the 28nm node. This test case is part of the ongoing qualification program for the Zeta-388 platform.
sections.2_SCOPE:
- Product Line: Zeta-388
- Inspection Type: Particle Detection
- Target Defect: Delamination
- Process Step: Post-Planarization
- Wafer Size: 300mm
- Technology Node: 28nm
- Fab Location: Hsinchu Fab 15

This test case applies to all Zeta-388 systems deployed at Hsinchu Fab 15 for post-planarization monitoring in the 28nm manufacturing line. Results from this test are used to establish baseline performance metrics and to qualify new recipe configurations.
sections.3_TEST_CONFIGURATION:
System: Zeta-388
Software Version: v15.1.978
Recipe: PARTICLE_DETECTION_28nm_POST_PLANARIZATION
Illumination Mode: Brightfield
Scan Speed: Low (53 mm/s)
Pixel Size: 0.5μm
Edge Exclusion: 5mm
Sampling Plan: 21-point sampling
sections.4_TEST_PROCEDURE:
1. Power on the Zeta-388 system and allow 30-minute warm-up period.
2. Load the calibration wafer and run the standard calibration routine.
3. Verify calibration results are within specification (±2% tolerance).
4. Load the test wafer onto the stage using the automated handler.
5. Select the 'Particle Detection' recipe from the recipe library.
6. Configure detection sensitivity to target Delamination defects.
7. Set scan parameters: full wafer scan with edge exclusion of 3mm.
8. Initiate the inspection run and monitor real-time defect map.
9. Upon completion, review the defect density map and classification results.
10. Export results to the factory automation system (SECS/GEM interface).
11. Compare results against the golden reference baseline.
12. Document any anomalies and generate the summary report.
sections.5_ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA:
- Defect detection sensitivity must meet 28nm node requirements
- False positive rate shall not exceed 5% of total detected events
- Scan throughput must be ≥ 73 wafers per hour
- Classification accuracy shall be ≥ 96% for known defect types
- Repeatability (3-sigma) shall be within ±0.6% for Particle Detection
- System uptime during test shall be ≥ 98%
- All results must be traceable through the MES integration
- Measurement correlation with reference tool shall be ≥ 0.96 R²
sections.6_TEST_RESULTS:
Test Execution Date: 2025-05-26
Wafers Tested: 16
Total Defects Found: 788
Defect Density: 111.48 defects/cm²
Nuisance Rate: 1.4%
Capture Rate: 90.2%
Test Duration: 236 minutes
System Uptime: 98.5%

Result Classification: FAIL
sections.7_OBSERVATIONS:
a) The Zeta-388 demonstrated below-target performance in detecting Delamination at the 28nm node.

b) The capture rate exceeded the minimum threshold, confirming system readiness.

c) Nuisance rate is within acceptable limits.

d) No significant drift was observed during the test duration.

e) Recipe portability between systems at this fab was confirmed.
sections.8_CORRECTIVE_ACTIONS:
The following corrective actions are recommended:

1. Re-tune detection algorithm thresholds for Delamination at 28nm node.
2. Schedule follow-up test after recipe optimization.
3. Escalate to R&D for algorithm enhancement if re-tuning does not resolve sensitivity gap.
